episodic_summary:
As of 23 July, 2023, Jon greets Gina, mentioning that they haven't talked in a few days. Jon shares that he has been rehearsing hard and working on business plans, which he finds stressful, but he states that dancing has kept him going. Gina responds enthusiastically, encouraging Jon to push through and reach the point where others would quit, urging him to "just do it." Jon humorously acknowledges Gina's motivational words and asks who originally said them. Gina reveals that the phrase belongs to Shia LaBeouf. Jon laughs and confirms that it is indeed LaBeouf. Gina continues by emphasizing the importance of having a creative space for dancers, recalling her experience at dance class with a group of friends the previous Friday. She expresses confidence that Jon's studio will become a go-to spot for self-expression and encourages him to keep up the good work while not forgetting his passion for dance. Jon expresses gratitude for Gina's encouraging words, stating that they keep him motivated and that he can't wait for the studio to start welcoming dancers of all ages and backgrounds. Gina expresses happiness that her words are motivating Jon and offers her support, reminding him that every step brings him closer to his dream and to never give up. Jon reassures Gina that he won't quit and will keep going, no matter what challenges arise. Gina reminds Jon once more to "do it," to which Jon enthusiastically responds, "JUST DOING IT!" Gina concludes the conversation by affirming Jon's spirit and saying goodbye. 
Images: "[Gina] shows a photo of a group of dancers on a stage with their arms in the air" and "[Gina] shows a photo of three girls in ballet costumes sitting on a desk."

episodic_summary: As of 13 September, 2023, Caroline expresses to Melanie that she is inspired by seeing her work make a difference for the LGBTQ+ community, stating that knowing she is helping create a more loving world is amazing. Caroline expresses gratitude for her friends, family, and mentors' support, which inspires her to keep making art. Melanie praises Caroline's work, stating that it looks awesome and reflects the togetherness and power Caroline is talking about. Melanie inquires how long Caroline has been creating art. Caroline reveals that she has been creating art since she was 17 years old, describing it as empowering and cathartic, and noting how amazing it is that art can express things that are hard to put into words. Melanie shares that she has been into art for seven years and finally found her real muses in painting and pottery, describing it as calming and satisfying. Melanie shares a photo of a group of bowls and a starfish on a white surface, showcasing her pottery creation. Caroline admires the bowls, stating that they are amazing and each has cool designs. Caroline expresses her love for Melanie's choice of pottery as her art form, sharing that painting and drawing helped her express her feelings and explore her gender identity. Caroline emphasizes that creating art has been important to her during her transition, helping her understand and accept herself, for which she is very grateful. Melanie agrees, stating that art is both a creative outlet and a form of therapy, and asks Caroline if she has ever thought about trying pottery or another art form. Caroline responds that she has not done pottery yet but is open to trying new art forms, sharing a photo of a painting on an easel with a red and blue background. Melanie praises Caroline's painting, stating that she loves the red and blue colors and asks what inspired the idea behind it. Caroline explains that she made the painting to show her path as a trans woman, using red and blue to represent the binary gender system, while the mix of colors symbolizes smashing rigid thinking. Caroline concludes by stating that the painting is a reminder to love her authentic self, noting that it has taken a while to get to this point, but she is finally proud of who she is. Melanie expresses her admiration for Caroline's progress and pride in being her true self.
